title.zh: 卷23 衛操 莫含 劉庫仁
title.en: Volume 23: Wei Cao, Mo Han, Liu Kuren
title.raw: 卷23 衛操 莫含 劉庫仁 Volume 23: Wei Cao, Mo Han, Liu Kuren

sentences.zh: 衛操 莫含 劉庫仁

translations.literal: Wei Cao; Mo Han; Liu Kuren
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Wei Cao, Mo Han, and Liu Kuren

translations.literal: Wei Cao, styled Deyuan, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cao, whose style was Deyuan, came from Dai.

translations.literal: In youth he mastered chivalry and possessed talent and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he lived by the code of the knight-errant and showed both talent and strategic mind.

sentences.zh: 晉征北將軍衞瓘以操為牙門將，數使於國，頗自結附。

translations.literal: Jin General Who Pacifies the North Wei Guan made Cao a gate officer; he was repeatedly sent to the state and rather attached himself on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's General Who Pacifies the North, Wei Guan, appointed Cao gate officer and often sent him on missions to the Dai state, where Cao gradually built ties of his own.

sentences.zh: 始祖崩後，與從子雄及其宗室鄉親姬澹等十數人，同來歸國，說桓穆二帝招納晉人，於是晉人附者稍眾。

translations.literal: After the founding ancestor died, together with his nephew Xiong and more than ten clansmen and fellow-townsmen such as Ji Dan, he came in a body to return to the state, urging the Huan and Mu emperors to recruit Jin people; thereafter those of Jin who attached themselves grew somewhat numerous.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding ancestor passed away, Cao came home with his nephew Xiong and a dozen-odd kinsmen and neighbors, among them Ji Dan, and urged the Huan and Mu emperors to welcome Jin subjects. From then on Jin adherents grew steadily in number.

sentences.zh: 桓帝嘉之，以為輔相，任以國事。

translations.literal: Emperor Huan commended this and made him chief minister, entrusting him with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan approved and named him chief minister, charging him with the affairs of the realm.

sentences.zh: 及劉淵、石勒之亂，勸桓帝匡助晉氏。

translations.literal: When the disorders of Liu Yuan and Shi Le arose, he urged Emperor Huan to support and aid the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuan and Shi Le threw the north into rebellion, he pressed Emperor Huan to stand with the house of Jin.

sentences.zh: 東瀛公司馬騰聞而善之，表加將號。

translations.literal: Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command, hearing of it, approved and memorialized to add military titles.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command, hearing this, praised the policy and memorialized the throne to grant Cao further military rank.

sentences.zh: 稍遷至右將軍，封定襄侯。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Right General and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to Right General and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 桓帝崩後，操立碑於大邗城南，[1]以頌功德，云：「魏，軒轅之苗裔。

translations.literal: After Emperor Huan died, Cao erected a stele south of Da Hang city, [1] to praise his merit and virtue, saying: "Wei, a scion of Xuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Huan's death, Cao set up a monument south of Da Hang and [1], to hymn his achievements, began: "The Wei are offspring of the Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan.

sentences.zh: 」言：桓穆二帝「馳名域外，九譯宗焉。

translations.literal: " It says of the Huan and Mu emperors: "Their fame gallops beyond the borders; nine tongues pay them homage.
translations.idiomatic: " Of the Huan and Mu emperors it reads: "Their renown rides beyond the frontier; peoples of nine interpreters bow to them.

translations.literal: Governing the state and ruling the masses, awe and prohibition go forth in full force.
translations.idiomatic: In ruling the realm and commanding the people, their majesty and law ran everywhere.

translations.literal: Their sound stands out among the Hua tribes; they share radiance with pure numen.
translations.idiomatic: Their name shone among the Chinese lineages and matched the light of highest spirit.

sentences.zh: 智深謀遠，窮幽極明，治則清斷，沉浮得情。

translations.literal: Wisdom deep, plans far-reaching, probing the hidden and reaching the utmost bright; in governing, clear judgment; in rise and fall, grasping the heart of things.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in wisdom, far in counsel, they sounded the dark and touched the farthest light; in rule they were lucid and decisive, and in fortune's turns they read the truth of each case.

translations.literal: Benevolence like the spring sun; awesomeness like autumn's frost.
translations.idiomatic: Their grace was the spring sun; their sternness, autumn frost.

translations.literal: The strong did not bully the weak; they hid away care for the orphaned and alone.
translations.idiomatic: The mighty did not crush the meek; they sheltered orphans and the forsaken.

translations.literal: The Way taught benevolent conduct; they transformed without punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The Way they taught was humane action; they changed hearts without the lash.

translations.literal: Within the state no treachery or theft; on the roads, songs of praise.
translations.idiomatic: No traitor or thief walked the land; along the roads people sang their praise.

translations.literal: From west to east, change without form.
translations.idiomatic: From west to east their influence shifted like formless change.

translations.literal: Wherever martial might was aimed, below them no armies crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Where their arms pointed, no foe dared meet them in the field.

translations.literal: South they unified the royal house; north they made the Dingling submit.
translations.idiomatic: To the south they upheld the imperial house; to the north they brought the Dingling to heel.

translations.literal: They summoned and instructed the six Di; all came in returning sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: They called and taught the six Di peoples, and all returned in good faith.

translations.literal: Surpassing what went before and cutting off what came after, they brought this achievement to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Outdoing the past and unmatched thereafter, they brought this triumph into being.

translations.literal: They upheld the Jin emperor and defended the frontier borders.
translations.idiomatic: They served the Jin sovereign and held the marches against invasion.

translations.literal: The royal house had many hardships; heaven's net slackened its cords.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial house knew many calamities; the net of heaven hung loose.

translations.literal: With heroic hearts they aided from afar and did not leave its afflictions.
translations.idiomatic: With heroic hearts they aided from afar and would not abandon Jin in its ruin.

translations.literal: Year by year they cut down rebellious fate; traitors and thieves were wolves and jackals.
translations.idiomatic: Each year they struck down rebellion; traitors and bandits prowled like wolves.

translations.literal: Yong'an year one, the year star at jiazi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yong'an, the cycle stood at jiazi.

translations.literal: The traitor faction still rebelled; east and west wolves stood at bay.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel clique still defied the throne; east and west, foes crouched like wolves.

translations.literal: They dared press the Son of Heaven; arms and armor rose again and again.
translations.idiomatic: They dared harry the Son of Heaven; war flared up time after time.

translations.literal: Relying on their numbers they indulged in violence and cruelly used the commanders and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting their numbers, they rampaged and abused officers and men.

translations.literal: Ye and Luoyang met with rifts; they cast off kin to seek the distant.
translations.idiomatic: Ye and Luoyang split in discord; they forsook their own to court strangers.

translations.literal: Then they recruited violent sorts—the Tuge and the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Then they called in savage allies: the Tuge and the Xiongnu.

translations.literal: Liu Yuan the traitorous villain banded with them in common cry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan the renegade joined their faction and shouted with one voice.

translations.literal: They dared strike Bing province and slaughter the guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: They dared strike into Bing and slaughter the innocent.

translations.literal: Ruin and breakage lay like scattered reeds; cities and towns became mounds and ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Devastation spread like trampled fields; towns were heaped into rubble.

translations.literal: Blades crossed for a thousand li; a long serpent blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: For a thousand li blades crossed; a long serpent of war choked the highways.

translations.literal: Jin's Way answered heaven; its words unfolded good plans.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's mandate answered heaven; its counsel opened sound designs.

sentences.zh: 使持節、平北將軍、并州刺史、護匈奴中郎將、東瀛公司馬騰，才神絕世，規略超遠。

translations.literal: Bearer of the staff of office, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Bing province, Protector of the Xiongnu, Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command—talent and spirit unmatched in the age, strategy and layout surpassing the far horizon.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command—Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Bing, Protector of the Xiongnu—was a genius without peer, his designs reaching beyond the horizon.

translations.literal: The times met with many hardships; he feared harm to the imperial sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster piled upon disaster; he feared the altars of Jin would fall.

translations.literal: He wished to lead troops forth; the Xianyun burned fierce.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to march out with his host, but the northern Xianyun raged fierce.

translations.literal: He devised expedient measures and plans to aid the hardship with wondrous thought.
translations.idiomatic: He forged expedients and strange counsel to break the siege of calamity.

translations.literal: He wished to summon outside rescue; the court ministers none responded.
translations.idiomatic: He sought aid from beyond the court, but no minister at court would answer.

translations.literal: With high calculation he decided alone and settled the plan of alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Alone he weighed the heights and fixed the plan of alliance.

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the foreign state to lead troops within as reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Then he charged the outer state to bring its armies in as a reserve within.

translations.literal: He selected worthy men and chose knights and appointed them envoys of this good mission.
translations.idiomatic: He chose the able and picked knights and named them bearers of this charge.

sentences.zh: 遣參軍壺倫、牙門中行嘉、義陽亭侯衞謨、協義亭侯衞鞬等，馳奉檄書，至晉陽城。」

translations.literal: He sent Staff Officer Hu Lun, gate officer Zhonghang Jia, Marquis of Yiyang Ting Wei Mo, Marquis of Xieyi Ting Wei Jian, and others, galloping with the proclamation document to Jinyang city."
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Staff Officer Hu Lun, gate officer Zhonghang Jia, Marquis of Yiyang Ting Wei Mo, Marquis of Xieyi Ting Wei Jian, and others to race the imperial summons to Jinyang."

sentences.zh: 又稱：桓穆二帝「心在宸極。

translations.literal: Again it says of the Huan and Mu emperors: "Their hearts were at the polar throne.
translations.idiomatic: Again of the Huan and Mu emperors: "Their hearts clung to the imperial pole.

translations.literal: The two Weis as chief ministers faced and raised, wing to wing.
translations.idiomatic: The two Wei ministers stood as paired wings to lift the throne.

translations.literal: Cao unfolded literary stratagems; Xiong roused martial valor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao laid out plans in letters; Xiong flamed in deeds of war.

translations.literal: Receiving the command they met in council; in consultation and debate they blazed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to council, they debated with fire in their speech.

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi aided and his merit stood out in the Zhou house.
translations.idiomatic: Of old Duke Huan of Qi had aided the throne, and his merit shone in the annals of Zhou.

translations.literal: Illustrious names were loaded on the registers; ranks of reward and full gifts were complete.
translations.idiomatic: His fame filled the records; rewards and gifts were heaped upon him.

translations.literal: The great host turned and moved; splendor gathered like spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The great army wheeled into motion; glory gathered as though spirits had convened.

translations.literal: They raised an army of a million; the term was not to pass a single day.
translations.idiomatic: They mustered a million men, promising victory within a day.

translations.literal: Brothers in one pact, they decided victory in the temple's calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers bound in one oath, they settled victory in the war council of the temple.

translations.literal: Beating drums and clamor they marched south and leveled the perilous and hard."
translations.idiomatic: With drums and battle-cry they marched south and smoothed away danger and hardship."

sentences.zh: 又云：二帝到鎮，「言若合符。

translations.literal: Again it says: when the two emperors reached their command post, "words like matching tallies.
translations.idiomatic: It adds: when the two emperors took the field, "their words matched like split tally-sticks.

translations.literal: They drew in with intimate good faith; trust and righteousness never shifted.
translations.idiomatic: They received each other in close trust; faith and duty never wavered.

translations.literal: They allied east of the Fen and inscribed the covenant in cinnabar script.
translations.idiomatic: They swore alliance east of the Fen and cut the oath in vermilion on stone.

translations.literal: Forever to uphold and serve; careful at the end as at the first.
translations.idiomatic: To serve forever; to guard the bond at the end as at the beginning.

translations.literal: The covenant charged the generals; elite sharpness led the van.
translations.idiomatic: The sworn pact set the generals marching; picked warriors rode in the van.

translations.literal: South they rescued Nie county; east they relieved Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Southward they relieved Nie; eastward they broke the siege of Shouyang.

translations.literal: Straitened towns, darkened, then shone again with light.
translations.idiomatic: Cities that had sunk into darkness burned bright again.

sentences.zh: 太原、西河，樂平、上黨，遽遭寇暴，白骨交橫。

translations.literal: Taiyuan, Xihe, Leping, and Shangdang suddenly met with bandit violence; white bones lay crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan, Xihe, Leping, and Shangdang were suddenly ravaged; the dead lay in crossed heaps of bone.

translations.literal: The Jie bandits ran wild; the six commanderies withered in harm.
translations.idiomatic: Jie raiders ran riot; six commanderies were laid waste.

translations.literal: The wicked in throngs answered one another; their plot reached the splendid hall.
translations.idiomatic: Evil men answered one another in crowds; their plot aimed at the throne room itself.

translations.literal: Banners and flags lightly pointed; the Jie faction broke and perished.
translations.idiomatic: At a light signal of banners the Jie hosts shattered and fell.

translations.literal: They sent ten thousand horsemen to advance before them to the Qi and Zhang rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand horsemen were sent ahead to the banks of the Qi and Zhang.

translations.literal: Ye then shook apart and collapsed; the vicious rebels ran and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ye shook apart and collapsed; the traitors fled in rout.

translations.literal: The army held the south of the province; their gleaming blades faced the Taihang.
translations.idiomatic: The army held the southern commanderies; their bright spears pointed at the Taihang.

translations.literal: Wing and guard within and without; they quieted the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: They shielded the realm within and without and stilled the four quarters.

translations.literal: Their will was to exhaust their strength and uphold and carry the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Their will was to spend their last strength upholding the Son of Heaven.

translations.literal: Loyalty and forbearance shone forth; stirred from without, they also repelled.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and forbearance lit the age; stirred from without, they drove the foe back as well.

translations.literal: [2] Thereupon they displayed martial might and, shaking the host, turned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Then they flaunted their arms, rallied the columns, and marched home.

translations.literal: The long road was not of the Yi; going out and entering took a full year.
translations.idiomatic: The road was long and strange; their going and coming spanned a year.

translations.literal: Not a hair was violated; the common people spread their praise.
translations.idiomatic: Not a hair of the people was harmed; folk praised them on every tongue.

translations.literal: They perused the loaded records from antiquity down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: They searched the loaded annals from antiquity to their own day.

translations.literal: They had not heard of an outer domain rushing to rescue an inner affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Never had they read of a border people racing inward to save an imperial crisis.

translations.literal: They abandoned family and grieved for the state, exchanging danger for peace.
translations.idiomatic: They left their homes and grieved for the realm, trading peril for peace.

translations.literal: Only the duke's far-reaching layout—in facing hardship could wield power.
translations.idiomatic: Only the lord's far sight—in hardship he still held authority.

translations.literal: Answering heaven and following the people, grace and virtue long proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: He answered heaven and followed the people; grace and virtue had long been proclaimed.

translations.literal: He harmonized the Rong and quieted the north; the endangered state was restored."
translations.idiomatic: He made peace with the Rong and stilled the north; the realm in peril lived again."

sentences.zh: 又云：桓帝經濟，「存亡繼絕。

translations.literal: Again it says of Emperor Huan's governance: "He preserved what was perishing and continued what was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Again of Emperor Huan's rule: "He preserved the dying line and continued what had been severed.

translations.literal: The wild domains relied on him; the throne endured without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: The far marches leaned on him; the throne endured unbroken.

translations.literal: Golden tortoise, reed-pipes and drums, light carriages and special regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Golden tortoise insignia, reed-pipes and drums, light carriages and marks of special honor.

translations.literal: Reaching back to the two dynasties, none stood in the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back through two dynasties, none shared his rank.

translations.literal: The Bing region sighed in praise; the northern states felt his glory.
translations.idiomatic: Bing province sighed in praise; the northern lands felt his glory.

translations.literal: Each exhausted his heart, thinking to raise his fine name.
translations.idiomatic: Each gave his whole heart, eager to lift his noble name.

translations.literal: They carved stone to record merit; images preserved his form.
translations.idiomatic: They carved stone to record his deeds; painted images kept his likeness.

translations.literal: Without ceasing they offered sacrifice; they feasted him with victims.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice never ceased; victims were set before him in feast.

translations.literal: Forever handed down to later ages; when gone, no remnant spirit was left.
translations.idiomatic: His fame was handed down forever; in death no shade of him was lost.

translations.literal: Long preserved without decay; extended for a hundred million ages."
translations.idiomatic: He endures undying; his glory stretches through ages beyond counting."

sentences.zh: 皇興初，雍州別駕雁門段榮於大邗掘得此碑，文雖非麗，事宜載焉，故錄於傳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangxing, Duan Rong of Yanmen, Assistant in Yong province, dug up this stele at Da Hang; though the text is not beautiful, the matter ought to be recorded, and therefore it is copied into the biography.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huangxing era, Duan Rong of Yanmen, assistant administrator of Yong province, unearthed this stele at Da Hang. The writing is not elegant, but the events deserve record, and so they are set down here in the biography.

translations.literal: The Huan and Mu emperors both honored Cao with ritual weight.
translations.idiomatic: Both Emperor Huan and Emperor Mu treated Cao with high ceremonial honor.

translations.literal: In Emperor Mu's third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Emperor Mu.

sentences.zh: 始操所與宗室鄉親入國者：衞懃，安樂亭侯；

translations.literal: At first, among the clansmen and fellow-townsmen who entered the state with Cao: Wei Qin, Marquis of Anle Ting;
translations.idiomatic: Those who had first entered the state with Cao among his kinsmen and neighbors included Wei Qin, Marquis of Anle Ting;

translations.literal: Wei Chong and Wei Qing, both Marquises of Du Ting;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chong and Wei Qing were both enfeoffed as Marquises of Du Ting;

sentences.zh: 衞泥、段繁，並信義將軍、都亭侯；

translations.literal: Wei Ni and Duan Fan, both Generals of Trust and Righteousness and Marquises of Du Ting;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ni and Duan Fan held the rank of General of Trust and Righteousness and were Marquises of Du Ting;

translations.literal: Wang Fa, General Who Establishes Martial Might and Marquis of Du Ting;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fa was made General Who Establishes Martial Might and Marquis of Du Ting;

sentences.zh: 范班，折衝將軍、廣武亭侯；

translations.literal: Fan Ban, General Who Breaks the Enemy and Marquis of Guangwu;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ban held the rank of General Who Breaks the Enemy and Marquis of Guangwu;

sentences.zh: 賈慶，建武將軍、上洛亭侯；

translations.literal: Jia Qing, General Who Establishes Martial and Marquis of Shangluo;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Qing was General Who Establishes Martial and Marquis of Shangluo;

translations.literal: Jia Xun, Commandery Marquis;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xun held commandery marquis rank;

translations.literal: Li Yi, Marquis of Guanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi was enfeoffed Marquis of Guanzhong;

translations.literal: Guo Ru, Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ru held the title Marquis Within the Passes.

translations.literal: All were enfeoffed and appointed by tables from Emperor Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Each had received rank and title from Emperor Huan's commendations.

sentences.zh: 六脩之難，存者多隨劉琨任子遵南奔。

translations.literal: In the trouble of Six Xiu, most of those who survived followed Liu Kun's heir-son Ziyun in flight south.
translations.idiomatic: After the Six Xiu disaster, most survivors fled south with Ren Ziyun, Liu Kun's designated heir.

sentences.zh: 衞雄、姬澹、莫含等名，皆見碑。

translations.literal: The names of Wei Xiong, Ji Dan, Mo Han, and others all appear on the stele.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiong, Ji Dan, Mo Han, and others are all named on the monument.

sentences.zh: 雄字世遠，澹字世雅，並勇健多計畫，晉世州從事。

translations.literal: Xiong's style was Shiyuan, Dan's style Shiya; both were brave and strong and full of stratagems, Jin-era provincial aides.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong styled himself Shiyuan and Dan Shiya; both were bold, resourceful men who had served as provincial aides under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 既與衞操俱入國，桓帝壯其膂力，並以為將，常隨征伐，大著威名。

translations.literal: After they entered the state together with Wei Cao, Emperor Huan admired their physical strength and made them both generals; they constantly followed on campaign and won great renown.
translations.idiomatic: When they entered the realm with Wei Cao, Emperor Huan was impressed by their strength and made them generals; they fought at his side on campaign after campaign and won a towering reputation.

sentences.zh: 桓帝之赴難也，表晉列其勳效，皆拜將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huan went to relieve the crisis, he memorialized the Jin court listing their achievements, and all were appointed generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huan marched to the rescue, he reported their deeds to the Jin court and secured general's commissions for them all.

sentences.zh: 雄連有戰功，稍遷至左將軍、雲中侯。

translations.literal: Xiong repeatedly won in battle and was gradually promoted to Left General and Marquis of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong piled victory on victory until he rose to Left General and Marquis of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 澹亦以勇績著名，桓帝末，至信義將軍、樓煩侯。

translations.literal: Dan too was famed for courage in action; at the end of Emperor Huan's reign he reached General of Faith and Righteousness and Marquis of Loufan.
translations.idiomatic: Dan likewise became famous for martial feats; by the close of Emperor Huan's reign he held General of Faith and Righteousness and Marquis of Loufan.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Mu's reign both were entrusted with office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Mu's reign both were again given weighty trust.

sentences.zh: 衞操卒後，俱為左右輔相。

translations.literal: After Wei Cao died, both became left and right assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Cao's death they served together as the left and right hands of government.

sentences.zh: 六脩之逆，國內大亂，新舊猜嫌，迭相誅戮。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Six Xiu the state fell into great disorder; old and new factions nursed suspicion and slaughtered one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Xiu revolt threw the realm into chaos; old settlers and new allies eyed one another with suspicion and killed in waves.

sentences.zh: 雄、澹並為羣情所附，謀欲南歸，言於眾曰：「聞諸舊人忌新人悍戰，欲盡殺之，吾等不早為計，恐無種矣。

translations.literal: Xiong and Dan were both attached to by the multitude; they plotted to flee south and said to the assembly: "We hear the old hands resent the newcomers' fierceness in battle and mean to kill them all; if we do not plan early, I fear our line will perish.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd rallied to Xiong and Dan; they planned a southern flight and told the assembly, "We hear the old faction hates how fiercely the newcomers fight and intends to wipe them out. Unless we act now, our line will end."

sentences.zh: 」晉人及烏丸驚懼，皆曰：「死亡隨二將軍。

translations.literal: " Jin men and Wuhuan were alarmed and afraid, and all said: "Death follows the two generals.
translations.idiomatic: " Jin subjects and Wuhuan alike were terrified and cried, "We live or die with these two generals."

sentences.zh: 」於是雄、澹與劉琨任子遵率烏丸、晉人數萬眾而叛。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xiong and Dan with Liu Kun's heir-son Ziyun led tens of thousands of Wuhuan and Jin men in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: " Then Xiong and Dan, with Ren Ziyun, Liu Kun's heir, led tens of thousands of Wuhuan and Jin followers into open revolt.

sentences.zh: 琨聞之大悅，率數百騎馳如平城撫納之。

translations.literal: Kun heard and was greatly pleased; he led several hundred horsemen at full gallop to Pingcheng to receive and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun was overjoyed at the news and raced to Pingcheng with a few hundred horsemen to welcome and settle them.

sentences.zh: 會石勒攻琨樂平，太守韓據請救於琨。

translations.literal: It happened that Shi Le attacked Kun's Le'ping; the prefect Han Ju requested rescue from Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Shi Le struck Liu Kun at Le'ping; the prefect Han Ju begged Liu Kun for relief.

sentences.zh: 琨以得雄、澹之眾，欲因其銳，以滅石勒。

translations.literal: Kun, having gained the hosts of Xiong and Dan, wished to use their sharp edge to destroy Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun, now reinforced by Xiong and Dan's troops, meant to hurl that fresh strength against Shi Le and destroy him.

sentences.zh: 雄、澹諫曰：「亂民飢疲，未可便用，宜休息觀釁而動。

translations.literal: Xiong and Dan remonstrated, saying: "The disorderly masses are hungry and weary and cannot yet be used; it is fit to rest, watch for openings, and then move.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and Dan urged caution: "These men are hungry, exhausted rebels—not yet fit to throw into battle. Rest them, watch for an opening, then strike."

sentences.zh: 」琨不從，使雄、澹率眾討勒，琨屯廣牧為之聲援。

translations.literal: " Kun would not follow; he sent Xiong and Dan to lead the host against Le; Kun encamped at Guangmu to sound support.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Kun refused. He sent Xiong and Dan against Le while he held Guangmu to back them.

sentences.zh: 勒率輕騎與雄、澹戰，澹大敗，率騎千餘，奔于代郡。

translations.literal: Le led light cavalry to battle Xiong and Dan; Dan was utterly defeated and fled with more than a thousand horsemen to Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le met them with light cavalry; Dan was routed and fled north with a thousand riders into Dai.

translations.literal: Le sent Kong Chang in pursuit to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Le sent Kong Chang in pursuit to finish him off.

translations.literal: Mo Han was a man of Fanzhi in Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Han came from Fanzhi in Yanmen.

translations.literal: His family for generations traded goods and amassed wealth in the tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: His family had traded for generations and piled up wealth beyond counting.

translations.literal: When Liu Kun held Bing province he summoned Han as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Kun governed Bingzhou he took Han on as an aide.

sentences.zh: 含居近塞下，常往來國中。

translations.literal: Han dwelt near the frontier and often came and went within the state.
translations.idiomatic: Han lived near the border and often traveled into the Tuoba realm.

translations.literal: Emperor Mu loved his talent and capacity and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu admired his ability and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 及為代王，備置官屬，求含於琨。

translations.literal: When he became Prince of Dai he fully set up officials and sought Han from Kun.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Prince of Dai he formed a full court and asked Liu Kun to send Han to him.

translations.literal: Kun sent him into the state; Han in his heart was unwilling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun sent him, but Han's heart was not in the move.

sentences.zh: 琨諭之曰：「當今胡寇滔天，泯滅諸夏，百姓流離，死亡塗地，主上幽執，沉溺醜虜。

translations.literal: Kun instructed him, saying: "Today the Hu raiders fill the sky, extinguishing the various Xia; the hundred surnames are displaced, death covers the ground, the sovereign is held in secret imprisonment, drowned among ugly captors.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun reasoned with him: "Barbarian armies now cover the sky and are snuffing out the Chinese realms; the people wander homeless, the roads are heaped with dead, and our emperor languishes in the hands of savage captors."

sentences.zh: 唯此一州，介在羣胡之間，以吾薄德，能自存立者，賴代王之力。

translations.literal: Only this one province stands among the mass of Hu; that I, with my slight virtue, can preserve myself and stand upright is because I rely on the Prince of Dai's strength.
translations.idiomatic: " Only this province still stands amid the barbarian tide; that I survive at all on my meager merit is because the Prince of Dai upholds me."

sentences.zh: 是以傾身竭寶，長子遠質，覬滅殘賊，報雪大耻。

translations.literal: Therefore I pour out body and treasure, send my eldest son far as hostage, and hope to extinguish the remnant bandits and wash away the great shame.
translations.idiomatic: " I have poured out my person and my wealth, sent my eldest son away as hostage, and staked everything on crushing the remnant enemy and avenging the realm's disgrace."

sentences.zh: 卿為忠節，亦是奮義之時，何得苟惜共事之小誠，以忘出身之大益。

translations.literal: You, as a man of loyal integrity, are also in a time to rouse righteousness; how can you be sparing of a small bond of service together and forget the great benefit of your own emergence?
translations.idiomatic: " You are a man of loyalty; this is the hour to act on it. How can you cling to a petty tie of service and forget the far greater good of stepping forward?"

sentences.zh: 入為代王腹心，非但吾願，亦一州所賴。

translations.literal: To enter and become the Prince of Dai's trusted center is not only my wish but also what one province relies upon.
translations.idiomatic: " To enter and become the prince's trusted confidant is not only my wish—it is what our whole province depends on."

translations.literal: " Han then entered Dai and took part in state office.
translations.idiomatic: " Han at last entered Dai and joined the government.

sentences.zh: 後琨徙五縣之民於陘南，含家獨留。

translations.literal: Later Kun moved the people of five counties south of the Xing ridge; Han's household alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Kun relocated five counties' people south of the Xing Mountains; Han's family alone stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 含甚為穆帝所重，常參軍國大謀。

translations.literal: Han was greatly valued by Emperor Mu and constantly took part in great plans of army and state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu held him in the highest regard and kept him at the heart of military and civil strategy.

translations.literal: He died in office as Left General and Marquis of Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He died holding Left General and Marquis of Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 其故宅在桑乾川南，世稱莫含壁，或音訛，謂之莫回城云。

translations.literal: His old residence lay south of the Sanggan River; the world calls it Mo Han's rampart, or through corrupted pronunciation Mo Hui City.
translations.idiomatic: His old house stood south of the Sanggan River; people still call the place Mo Han's Rampart—or, in a corrupted pronunciation, Mo Hui City.

translations.literal: His son Xian was famed in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian won renown in his own day.

translations.literal: In the Zhaocheng era he was made Left Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaocheng he became Left Palace Attendant.

translations.literal: Xian's son Ti also had stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's son Ti was likewise a man of counsel.

sentences.zh: 太祖使題與將軍王建等三軍，討慕容寶廣寧太守劉亢埿，斬之。

translations.literal: Taizu sent Ti with the general Wang Jian and the three armies to campaign against Murong Bao's Guangning prefect Liu Kangqi and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Ti with General Wang Jian and a three-wing army against Murong Bao's Guangning prefect Liu Kangqi and took his head.

translations.literal: Kangqi's tribes were moved to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kangqi's tribes were resettled at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 寶上谷太守驎，捐郡逃走，太祖追討，題為大將，別出東道。

translations.literal: Bao's Shanggu prefect Lin abandoned the commandery and fled; Taizu pursued in punishment; Ti was made grand general and marched out by the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's Shanggu prefect Lin deserted his commandery and fled; Taizu pursued him; Ti was made grand general and took a separate eastern road.

translations.literal: For merit he was given the enfeoffment Marquis of Dongwan.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dongwan.

sentences.zh: 及還京師，常與李栗侍宴。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital he constantly attended banquets with Li Li.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the capital he often shared the emperor's table with Li Li.

sentences.zh: 栗坐不敬獲罪，題亦被黜為濟陽太守。

translations.literal: Li was punished for irreverence in seating; Ti was also demoted to Administrator of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li was punished for disrespect at court; Ti was demoted as well, to administrator of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 後太祖欲廣宮室，規度平城四方數十里，將模鄴、洛、長安之制，運材數百萬根。

translations.literal: Later Taizu wished to enlarge the palaces and measured several tens of li around Pingcheng, intending to model Ye, Luoyang, and Chang'an; timber in the millions of logs was transported.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizu planned to expand the palace quarter, surveyed dozens of li around Pingcheng, and meant to imitate Ye, Luoyang, and Chang'an; millions of timbers were hauled in.

translations.literal: Because Ti was ingenious in mechanism he was summoned and ordered to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Ti's mechanical ingenuity won him summons to oversee the work.

translations.literal: He was called in and discussed the fitness of the construction.
translations.idiomatic: He was called in to debate the right scale and design of the build.

translations.literal: Ti after long attendance grew somewhat slack; he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: After long attendance Ti grew careless in his duties and was put to death.

translations.literal: Ti's younger brother Yun loved learning and was skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: Ti's younger brother Yun loved books and excelled at the bow.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，常典選曹，轉給事中。

translations.literal: In Taizu's time he constantly managed the Selection Bureau and was transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu he ran the Selection Bureau and later became palace attendant.

translations.literal: For merit he was given the enfeoffment Marquis of Ande.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Ande.

sentences.zh: 遷執金吾，常參軍國謀議。

translations.literal: He was promoted Commandant of Cavalry and constantly took part in deliberations on army and state.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Commandant of Cavalry and sat in on every major counsel of war and state.

sentences.zh: 世祖之克赫連昌，詔雲與常山王素留鎮統萬。

translations.literal: When Shizu captured Helian Chang, he edicted Yun and the Prince of Changshan Su to remain and garrison Tongwan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu took Helian Chang, he ordered Yun and Prince Su of Changshan to hold Tongwan.

sentences.zh: 進爵安定公，加平西將軍，後遷鎮西大將軍。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Anding, with added General Who Pacifies the West; later he was transferred Grand General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Anding and General Who Pacifies the West, then to Grand General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 時初并河西，人心未一，雲撫慰新舊，皆得其所。

translations.literal: At that time the Hexi region had just been annexed and hearts were not yet one; Yun comforted old and new alike and all found their place.
translations.idiomatic: The Hexi had only just been absorbed and loyalties were still divided; Yun soothed old subjects and new until each settled where he belonged.

translations.literal: He died in the Shenju era; posthumous title: Duke Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Shenju era and was posthumously titled Duke Reverent.

sentences.zh: 劉庫仁，本字沒根，劉虎之宗也，一名洛垂。

translations.literal: Liu Kuren, original style Meigen, was of the lineage of Liu Hu; he had another name, Lo Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuren, whose original name was Meigen, belonged to the house of Liu Hu and was also called Lo Chui.

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and open, with wisdom and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was open-handed and bold, with a strategist's mind.

translations.literal: His mother was a daughter of Emperor Pingwen.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was born a princess of Emperor Pingwen's house.

sentences.zh: 昭成皇帝復以宗女妻之，為南部大人。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaocheng again gave him a clanswoman in marriage and made him southern grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaocheng married him to another royal clanswoman and made him southern grandee.

sentences.zh: 建國三十九年，昭成暴崩，太祖未立，苻堅以庫仁為陵江將軍、關內侯，令與衞辰分國部眾而統之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year of Jianguo Emperor Zhaocheng died suddenly; Taizu was not yet established; Fu Jian made Kuren General Who Commands the River and Marquis Within the Passes and ordered him with Wei Chen to divide the state's tribes and rule them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianguo year 39 Emperor Zhaocheng died suddenly before Taizu could be enthroned; Fu Jian made Liu Kuren General Who Commands the River and Marquis Within the Passes and set him with Wei Chen to divide and govern the tribal following.

sentences.zh: 自河以西屬衞辰，自河以東屬庫仁。

translations.literal: From the river west belonged to Wei Chen; from the river east belonged to Kuren.
translations.idiomatic: West of the river fell to Wei Chen; east of the river to Liu Kuren.

sentences.zh: 於是獻明皇后攜太祖及衞秦二王自賀蘭部來居焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Empress Dowager Xianming brought Taizu and the two princes of Wei and Qin from the Helan tribe to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Then Empress Dowager Xianming brought Taizu and the Wei and Qin princes from the Helan tribe to live under Kuren's protection.

sentences.zh: 庫仁盡忠奉事，不以興廢易節，撫納離散，恩信甚彰。

translations.literal: Kuren served with full loyalty and did not change his constancy with rise or fall; he gathered and settled the scattered, and his favor and trust were greatly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuren served him with unwavering loyalty, never shifting with fortune's turns; he gathered the scattered and won them with grace, and his trustworthiness was plain to all.

sentences.zh: 苻堅進庫仁廣武將軍，給幢麾鼓蓋，儀比諸侯。

translations.literal: Fu Jian advanced Kuren to General of Guangwu, gave him banner, canopy, drums, and parasol, and ceremonial parity with feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian promoted him to General of Guangwu and granted the insignia of banner, canopy, drums, and parasol, with ceremony equal to a feudal lord.

translations.literal: Wei Chen was placed below Kuren.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chen was ranked beneath Liu Kuren.

sentences.zh: 衞辰怒，殺堅五原太守而叛，攻庫仁西部。

translations.literal: Wei Chen was enraged, killed Fu Jian's Administrator of Wuyuan, and rebelled, attacking Kuren's western territory.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chen flew into rage, murdered Fu Jian's administrator of Wuyuan, rebelled, and struck Liu Kuren's western lands.

sentences.zh: 庫仁又伐衞辰破之，追至陰山西北千餘里，獲其妻子，盡收其眾。

translations.literal: Kuren again campaigned against Wei Chen and defeated him, pursuing to more than a thousand li northwest of Yin Mountain, taking his wife and children and gathering all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuren counterattacked, broke Wei Chen, and chased him more than a thousand li beyond Yin Mountain, seizing his family and absorbing his entire following.

sentences.zh: 庫仁西征庫狄部，大獲畜產，徙其部落，置之桑乾川。

translations.literal: Kuren campaigned west against the Kudi tribe, took great herds and goods, moved their tribes, and settled them on the Sanggan River.
translations.idiomatic: He marched west against the Kudi, captured vast herds, relocated the tribe, and planted them along the Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 苻堅賜庫仁妻公孫氏，厚其資送。

translations.literal: Fu Jian bestowed on Kuren's wife the Gongsun clan and enriched her dowry and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian gave Liu Kuren's wife the surname Gongsun and loaded her with gifts.

sentences.zh: 庫仁又詣堅，加庫仁振威將軍。

translations.literal: Kuren again went to Jian and was further made General Who Quells Might.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuren went again to Fu Jian's court and was raised to General Who Quells Might.

sentences.zh: 後慕容垂圍苻丕于鄴，又遣將平規攻堅幽州刺史王永于薊，庫仁自以受堅爵命，遣妻兄公孫希率騎三千，助永擊規，大破之，阬規降卒五千餘人。

translations.literal: Later Murong Chui besieged Fu Pi at Ye and also sent a general, Ping Gui, to attack Fu Jian's Inspector of Youzhou Wang Yong at Ji; Kuren, holding himself bound by the titles Jian had granted, sent his wife's elder brother Gongsun Xi with three thousand horsemen to aid Yong in striking Gui; he utterly defeated him and pit-killed more than five thousand of Gui's surrendered soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui besieged Fu Pi at Ye and sent Ping Gui against Fu Jian's Youzhou inspector Wang Yong at Ji, Liu Kuren—still loyal to the titles Fu Jian had given him—sent his brother-in-law Gongsun Xi with three thousand horse to help Yong rout Gui and massacre more than five thousand of Gui's men who had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 乘勝長驅，進據唐城，與垂子麟相持。

translations.literal: Seizing victory he drove far, advanced and held Tangcheng, and stood in stalemate with Chui's son Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the victory he drove deep, seized Tangcheng, and locked horns with Chui's son Lin.

sentences.zh: 庫仁聞希破規，復將大舉以救丕。

translations.literal: Kuren heard Xi had broken Gui and again was about to raise a great host to rescue Pi.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Kuren heard Xi had crushed Gui, he gathered a great army to relieve Fu Pi.

sentences.zh: 發雁門、上谷、代郡兵，次於繁畤。

translations.literal: He mobilized the armies of Yanmen, Shanggu, and Dai commanderies and halted at Fanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He called up the forces of Yanmen, Shanggu, and Dai and camped at Fanzhi.

sentences.zh: 先是，慕容文等當徙長安，遁依庫仁部，常思東歸，其計無由。

translations.literal: Earlier, Murong Wen and others had been due for relocation to Chang'an; they had fled into hiding with Kuren's tribe and constantly thought of returning east, but had no means.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Murong Wen and others, slated for resettlement in Chang'an, had taken refuge with Liu Kuren's tribe and longed to go east again but saw no way.

sentences.zh: 至是役也，知人不樂，文等乃夜率三郡人，攻庫仁。

translations.literal: At this levy they knew men were discontent; Wen and the rest therefore by night led the people of three commanderies to attack Kuren.
translations.idiomatic: On this campaign they saw how little love the levy inspired; Wen and his party struck by night, leading men of three commanderies against Liu Kuren.

sentences.zh: 庫仁匿於馬廐，文執殺之。

translations.literal: Kuren hid in the horse stable; Wen seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuren hid in the stable; Wen seized him and killed him.

translations.literal: They took his swift horse and fled to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: They mounted his best horse and fled to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 公孫希聞亂，自唐城走於丁零。

translations.literal: Gongsun Xi heard of the turmoil and fled from Tangcheng to the Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Xi, hearing of the revolt, abandoned Tangcheng and fled to the Dingling.

translations.literal: Kuren's younger brother Juan succeeded to take charge of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuren's younger brother Juan stepped in to govern the tribes.

sentences.zh: 白部大人絜佛叛，[3]眷力不能討。

translations.literal: The White Division grandee Jiefu rebelled, [3] and Juan's strength could not subdue him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiefu, grandee of the White Division, rebelled, [3] and Juan lacked the force to crush him.

sentences.zh: 乃引苻堅并州刺史張蚝擊佛，破之。

translations.literal: He therefore drew in Fu Jian's Inspector of Bingzhou Zhang Hao to strike Jiefu and break him.
translations.idiomatic: He called in Fu Jian's Bingzhou inspector Zhang Hao, who defeated Jiefu.

sentences.zh: 眷又破賀蘭部于善無，又擊蠕蠕別帥肺渥于意親山，破之，獲牛羊數十萬頭。

translations.literal: Juan again broke the Helan tribe at Shanwu and also attacked the Rouran sub-chieftain Feiwo at Yiqin Mountain, defeated him, and took several hundred thousand head of cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Juan next routed the Helan at Shanwu and struck the Rouran sub-chief Feiwo at Yiqin Mountain, taking hundreds of thousands of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 眷第二子羅辰，性機警，有智謀，謂眷曰：「比來行兵，所向無敵，心腹之疾，願早圖之。

translations.literal: Juan's second son Luo Chen was by nature alert and possessed wisdom and stratagem; he said to Juan: "In recent campaigns wherever we marched we were without match; the trouble in our vitals—I wish we would plan for it early.
translations.idiomatic: Juan's second son Luo Chen was quick-witted and full of counsel; he told Juan, "Our armies have known no defeat—but the sickness is within. We should deal with it now."

translations.literal: " Juan said: "Who is it?
translations.idiomatic: " Juan asked, "Who?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「從兄顯，忍人也，為亂非旦則夕耳。

translations.literal: " He said: "Cousin Xian is a man who can endure; his rebellion will come not in the morning then in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Cousin Xian is ruthless. His revolt is only a matter of time."

translations.literal: " Juan did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: " Juan paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 其後，徙牧于牛川，庫仁子顯，果殺眷而代立。

translations.literal: Afterward, when the herds were moved to pasture at Niuchuan, Kuren's son Xian indeed killed Juan and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the herds were moved to Niuchuan, Liu Kuren's son Xian murdered Juan and usurped his place.

sentences.zh: 羅辰奔太祖，事在外戚傳。

translations.literal: Luo Chen fled to Taizu; the account is in the biography of the maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Chen fled to Taizu; the fuller account stands in the biography of the empresses' kin.

sentences.zh: 顯，本名醜伐，既殺眷代立，又欲謀逆，語在太祖紀。

translations.literal: Xian, original name Choufa, after killing Juan and replacing him also plotted rebellion; the words are in Taizu's annals.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, whose birth name was Choufa, after killing Juan and seizing rule plotted treason as well; that story is told in Taizu's annals.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，顯自善無南走馬邑。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Xian fled south from Shanwu to Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was enthroned, Xian fled south from Shanwu toward Mayi.

translations.literal: A clansman, Nuzhen, led his division in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Nuzhen, a kinsman of the line, brought his following in to submit.

translations.literal: Nuzhen's elder brother Jian had earlier dwelt with the Helan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Jian had long lived among the Helan.

sentences.zh: 至是，奴真請召犍而讓部焉。

translations.literal: At this time Nuzhen asked to summon Jian and yield the division to him.
translations.idiomatic: Now Nuzhen asked to call Jian in and turn the tribe over to him.

translations.literal: Taizu, moved by the righteousness of it, granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, approving the act, allowed it.

sentences.zh: 犍既領部，自以久託賀訥，德之，乃使弟去斤遺之金馬。

translations.literal: Once Jian held the division, deeming himself long indebted to He Ne for shelter, he sent his younger brother Qujin to present him with a golden horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian took command, he felt himself long beholden to He Ne and sent his brother Qujin with a gift of a golden horse.

sentences.zh: 訥弟染干因謂之曰：「我待汝兄弟厚，汝今領部，宜來從我。

translations.literal: He Ne's younger brother Ran'gan then said to him: "I have treated you brothers generously; now that you lead a division, you ought to come follow me."
translations.idiomatic: He Ne's brother Ran'gan told him, "I have been generous to you two; now that you lead a division, you should come over to my side."

translations.literal: Qujin asked Nuzhen about it.
translations.idiomatic: Qujin put the matter to Nuzhen.

sentences.zh: 奴真曰：「父為國家附臣，世効忠貞。

translations.literal: Nuzhen said: "Our father was a subject attached to the state; for generations we have served with loyal fidelity.
translations.idiomatic: Nuzhen replied, "Our father was the state's man; our house has served with loyalty for generations.

translations.literal: I sought to preserve our name and honor intact, and for that reason I yielded the division.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to keep our name whole, and that is why I yielded the tribe.

sentences.zh: 今汝等無狀，乃欲叛主懷貳。

translations.literal: Now you behave disgracefully and would betray your lord with divided hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Now you act shamefully and would turn traitor with a double heart."

translations.literal: He then killed Jian and Qujin.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Jian and Qujin on the spot.

sentences.zh: 染干聞其殺兄，率騎討之，奴真懼，徙部來奔太祖。

translations.literal: When Ran'gan heard that he had killed his elder brother, he led horsemen to attack him; Nuzhen in fear moved his division to flee to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Ran'gan, hearing his brother had been killed, led cavalry against him; Nuzhen in alarm moved his people to seek refuge with Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖自迎之，遣使責止染干。

translations.literal: Taizu went out in person to welcome him and sent envoys to reprimand Ran'gan and halt him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu rode out to meet him and sent envoys to rebuke Ran'gan and make him stop.

sentences.zh: 奴真感恩，請奉妹充後宮，太祖納之。

translations.literal: Grateful, Nuzhen offered his younger sister for the inner palace; Taizu took her.
translations.idiomatic: Nuzhen, moved by the grace shown him, offered his younger sister to the inner palace, and Taizu took her.

sentences.zh: 後太祖討顯于馬邑，追至彌澤，大破之。

translations.literal: Later Taizu campaigned against Xian at Mayi, pursued him to Mize, and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizu attacked Liu Xian at Mayi, chased him to Mize, and broke him completely.

sentences.zh: 衞辰與慕容垂通好，送馬三千匹於垂，垂遣慕容良迎之。

translations.literal: Wei Chen maintained friendly relations with Murong Chui and sent him three thousand horses; Chui dispatched Murong Liang to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chen was on good terms with Murong Chui and sent him three thousand horses; Chui sent Murong Liang to meet the herd.

translations.literal: Xian defeated Liang's army and seized the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian smashed Liang's force and drove off the horses.

sentences.zh: 垂怒，遣子麟、兄子楷討之，顯奔馬邑西山。

translations.literal: Chui in anger sent his son Lin and his brother's son Kai against him; Xian fled to the western hills of Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Chui in fury sent his son Lin and his brother's son Kai to punish him; Xian fled into the western hills of Mayi.

sentences.zh: 麟輕騎追之，遂奔慕容永於長子。

translations.literal: Lin with light cavalry pursued him, and he fled at last to Murong Yong at Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Lin pressed him with light horse until he took refuge with Murong Yong at Changzi.

sentences.zh: 部眾悉降於麟，麟徙之中山。

translations.literal: All his followers surrendered to Lin, and Lin resettled them at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His whole following submitted to Lin, and Lin moved them to Zhongshan.

translations.literal: Xian's younger brother Kang'ai: the account is in the Empresses' biography.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian's brother Kang'ai is treated in the Empresses' biography.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：始祖及桓、穆之世也，王迹初基，風德未展。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In the age of the Founding Ancestor and of the Huan and Mu emperors, the royal enterprise had only just been laid, and exemplary virtue was not yet fully displayed.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Under the Founding Ancestor and Emperors Huan and Mu, the royal work had barely begun and moral influence had not yet spread.

sentences.zh: 操、含託身馳驟之秋，自立功名之地，[4]可謂志識之士矣。

translations.literal: Cao and Han betook themselves to the season of galloping campaigns and made their own ground of merit and fame, [4] — men who may be called of purposeful mind and vision.
translations.idiomatic: Cao and Han threw themselves into the hurrying age of war and carved out a place of merit and renown, [4] — true men of purpose and sight.

sentences.zh: 劉庫仁兄弟，忠以為心，盛衰不二，純節所存，其意蓋遠，而並貽非命，惜乎！

translations.literal: The brothers Liu Kuren held loyalty as their heart; in fortune or decline they did not waver; the pure integrity they preserved showed purpose reaching far — yet both met untimely ends. A pity!
translations.idiomatic: The Liu Kuren brothers took loyalty for their heart and did not shift between rise and fall; the pure constancy they kept looked far ahead — yet both died before their time. What a loss!

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 操立碑於大邗城南 錢氏考異卷三八云：「此傳載衞操所立碑……惜為史臣改竄，失其本真。

translations.literal: Cao erected a stele south of Dahang city. Qian's Textual Notes, juan 38, state: "This biography records the stele Wei Cao erected" (the transmitted citation here abbreviates the middle) "Alas, the court historiographers altered it and its original truth was lost."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cao set up a stele south of Dahang city. In Qian's Textual Notes, juan 38, we read that this chapter preserves his inscription in full, yet the historiographers mangled the record and the authentic text was lost.

translations.literal: At the head of the inscription it reads: 'Scion of the Yellow Emperor of Wei.'
translations.idiomatic: The opening line runs, 'Scion of the Yellow Emperor of Wei.'

sentences.zh: 』考其時未有魏號，以文義度之當云『鮮卑拓跋氏』也。

translations.literal: On examination, at that time there was as yet no title of Wei; judged by the sense of the text it ought to read 'of the Xianbei Tuoba clan.'
translations.idiomatic: At that date there was no Wei designation yet; by sense it should read 'of the Xianbei Tuoba clan.'

sentences.zh: 碑為猗㐌而立，必書晉所授官爵及猗㐌、猗盧二人名，篇乃稱『桓穆二帝』，亦史臣所改。」

translations.literal: The stele was erected for Yiyi; it must have recorded the offices and ranks granted by Jin and the names of Yiyi and Yilu, yet the text calls them 'the two emperors Huan and Mu' — again an alteration by the historiographers."
translations.idiomatic: The stone was raised for Yiyi and must have named the Jin-bestowed offices and both Yiyi and Yilu; calling them 'the two emperors Huan and Mu' is another historiographer's change."

sentences.zh: 外動亦攘 北史卷二０本傳「動」作「勳」。

translations.literal: "In outward campaigns, he also repelled": in Northern History juan 20, this biography reads dong (campaign) as xun (merit).
translations.idiomatic: "Outward campaigns also repelled": Northern History juan 20, this life, has dong (campaign) for xun (merit).

sentences.zh: 按「外勳亦攘」，意為對外有攘患之功，碑末有「勳攘大患」句也是此意。

translations.literal: Commentary: "In outward merit he also repelled" means he had the achievement of repelling external calamity; the inscription's closing line "merit that repelled the great scourge" bears the same sense.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "outward merit also repelled" means merit in repelling foreign trouble; the stele's closing "merit that repelled the great scourge" is the same idea.

translations.literal: It seems xun (merit) is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Xun (merit) appears to be right.

sentences.zh: 白部大人絜佛叛 諸本「白」作「曰」。

translations.literal: "The great chief Jiefo of the Bai tribe rebelled": in various editions bai (white/Bai) is written as yue (say).
translations.idiomatic: "The Bai tribe's great chief Jiefo rebelled": editions read bai (Bai) as yue (say).

translations.literal: Cefu juan 352
translations.idiomatic: Cefu, juan 352

translations.literal: 〈page 4180〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 4180

translations.literal: reads "bai" (White/Bai).
translations.idiomatic: has "Bai."

sentences.zh: 按卷一序紀力微之三十九年稱：「夏四月祭天，諸部君長悉來助祭，唯白部大人觀望不至。

translations.literal: Commentary: Juan 1, Annalistic Preface, year 39 of Liwei states: "In the fourth month of summer they sacrificed to Heaven; the chieftains of all divisions came to assist in the rites — only the great chief of the Bai tribe stood apart and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Annalistic Preface, juan 1, Liwei year 39: "Fourth month, summer sacrifice to Heaven; every division's chief came to assist — only the Bai tribe's great chief held back and did not attend.

sentences.zh: 」又猗盧之三年稱「白部大人叛入西河」。

translations.literal: Again, year 3 of Yilu states "the great chief of the Bai tribe rebelled and entered Xihe."
translations.idiomatic: Yilu year 3 also says "the Bai tribe's great chief rebelled and entered Xihe."

translations.literal: The character yue is erroneous; the text is now emended according to Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: Yue is a corruption; emended per Cefu.

sentences.zh: 自立功名之地 諸本無「名」字。

translations.literal: "Made their own ground of merit and fame": various editions lack the character ming (fame/name).
translations.idiomatic: "Carved out a place of merit and renown": editions omit ming (fame).

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云：「『功』字下北史

translations.literal: Palace Edition textual notes state: "Below gong (merit) Northern History
translations.idiomatic: Palace Edition textual notes: "After gong (merit), Northern History

translations.literal: 〈juan 20〉
translations.idiomatic: (juan 20)

translations.literal: has the character ming; that reading should be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: has ming; that text should stand.

sentences.zh: 」按「功名」與上「馳驟」對文，這裏脫「名」字，今據北史補。

translations.literal: Commentary: "merit and fame" balances with "galloping" above; here the character ming has dropped out; supplied now according to Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "merit and fame" pairs with "hurrying" above; the word ming dropped here and is restored from the Northern History.
